design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (payment_arrangement_agreements, category arrange). Ids: member c4ed12e2-3be4-4b56-bee6-4245e4b0b014, house service account 8bcb40f7-c03e-47bf-9b5b-96e9b7139b8f, running agreement 2a82732f-cb50-4cfe-abc6-7809bb955e91, completed 2023 agreement f83148ff-5fe6-4680-8533-92c20a62f7bf.
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6, 4]. Missed-installment computation takes 6 factors, early payoff takes 4.
[Why a good test] Loretta Vance asks only to pay off her Extended Hardship plan. The payoff rule (arrange_ext_early_payoff_balance) carries the state-form prerequisite sentence 'The balance billed back on an early payoff is fixed only after every installment of the agreement whose grace period has ended unpaid carries a missed-installment entry on the agreement's ledger.' The ledger shows installment 3 (2026-09-01 bill, due 2026-09-21, grace 10 days -> ended 2026-10-01; installment 4 of 2026-10-01 is still inside its grace, so 3 is the latest installment whose grace has ended) unpaid and no missed entry, so the agent must first work the missed amount (six factors over service bill lines, payments, returns, pledges, the medical certificate and the capital account) and only then the payoff (four factors over credits, arrears, the certificate, capital and deposit records). Difficulty comes from discovering the miss and reconciling records, not from tool choice: there is one tool per write.
[Scope] Occupied before: nothing (first task). Claimed: arrange_ext_missed_installment_amount + arrange_ext_early_payoff_balance with tools book_missed_installment_8c48d67e (agent) and pay_off_payment_agreement_d76d2954 (user). Left for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisites): acceptance of a standing offer (the only other member-owned write), the balance transfer, installment billing and default, all untouched here.
[Problem-tree card] root arrange_ext_early_payoff_balance <- arrange_ext_missed_installment_amount; kind value_input, gate binding missed_month, form state; condition: every installment-billed entry whose due date + grace has passed unpaid has a matching missed entry; resolved_by book_missed_installment_8c48d67e (agent). Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; waits on a record-visible state (a missed-installment entry on the ledger); names no tool, id or code token; strength 'every installment ... whose grace period has ended unpaid' = the condition. Exactly one write of the difficulty creates missed-installment entries (book_missed_installment_8c48d67e), so the state->action hop is unique: sentence + ledger (no missed entry for installment 3) + the missed-installment rule ('An installment counts as missed when ...') -> book the miss. False at frozen_time: ledger rows of the agreement are one transfer and installments 1-4, none missed. Topological order: missed (step 11) then payoff (step 13). Deletion sensitivity (run below): skipping the miss gives payoff 151.09 instead of 201.67.
[Base-invariant card] arrange_installment_missed: governed by arrange_evt_default (eligibility []); its sentence 'An installment counts as missed when the installment, together with the current charges of the same bill ... is not paid in full within missed_installment_grace_days calendar days after that bill's due date' is superseded by a declared overwrite (tested lines, medical share, pledge credit, month window). Payoff (arrange_balance_rebill + arrange_complete): governed by arrange_evt_completion, arrange_evt_default and arrange_evt_termination (all eligibility []); the completion sentence on billing back the unbilled balance is superseded by a declared overwrite; early_payoff_allowed is true on the tier; no time gate applies to either subject (temporal_feasibility []).
[Business-object card] Target agreement 2a82732f-cb50-4cfe-abc6-7809bb955e91 (status active, Extended Hardship, accepted 2026-06-08). Missed: installment 3 entry (period 2026-09, 114.94); the 2023 agreement's ledger is excluded (other agreement). Payoff: unbilled = 689.61 moved in - 459.76 billed (4 x 114.94) - 0 billed back = 229.85 (arranged_balance agrees).
[Factor card, missed amount] current_lines_by_late_record (method): late charges 2026-03-22, 2026-06-22, 2026-09-22 within 12 months (2025-08-22 is the near-miss, outside) = 3 -> usage 206.01 + fee 30.00 + late 5.26 = 241.27; baseline usage only -> 32.95. medical_protection_share (parameter): certificate expires 2026-10-14, received 2026-09-14 (18 <= 30 days) -> 0.5; baseline 1 -> 171.21. payment_crediting_by_record (method): echeck 60.00 of 2026-09-10 returned 2026-09-15 -> 150.00 - 60.00 = 90.00; baseline 150.00 -> 0.00. pledge_lookback_by_circumstance (parameter, window length): unexpired certificate -> three months: 25.00 (2026-08-15) + 50.00 (2026-09-20) = 75.00; near-miss 2026-02-12 pledge outside; baseline one month 50.00 -> 75.58. pledge_credit_by_agency_record (parameter, multi-source): pledges counted AND LIHEAP agency payment 2026-03-18 within 12 months -> 1.0; baseline 0 -> 125.58. shortfall_allowance_by_standing (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty capital): no earlier miss AND capital account open 351 months (opened 1997-06-30, the June allocation that opened it) -> 20.00; baseline 0 -> 70.58. Whole baseline 170.95. Result 50.58 (50.575 rounded half up).
[Factor card, payoff] arrears_covered_first (method): the 50.58 missed entry recorded in the month, no notice -> covers 50.58 first; baseline nothing -> 151.09. credit_window_by_circumstance (parameter, window length; certificate and notice are fields of one service-account row, so not multi-source): unexpired certificate and no notice -> bill credits of the 11 months ending 2026-10-02; baseline the last month -> 229.85. capital_credit_share (parameter, cross-difficulty capital): Residential class active, 351 months -> 1.0 on the 69.24 general-retirement credit of the December 2025 bill (2025-12-01: the 2025 resolution approved 2025-11-18 - remaining 2003 margins, 18% of the 2018 margins and the 1998 G&T allocation - paid as a bill credit on the December bill, general_retirement_payment_month 12; 10 months back, so the 10-month window would miss it - near-miss); baseline 0 -> 229.85. deposit_interest_share (parameter, cross-difficulty deposit): held, paid in full 2024-09-24 (24 months) -> 1.0 on the 9.52 prior-year interest credit posted on the January 2026 bill (2025 interest = round(460.00 x 2.07% x 365/365, 2), the deposit tier's interest_payout_month 1); baseline 0 -> 211.19. Whole baseline 229.85. Result 201.67.
[Seed rows and why] 13 billing periods of usage lines (2025-10..2026-10, Schedule R rates 0.11840/0.10920, facility 32.50); late charges as above; the returned echeck and its 30.00 fee; pledges and the agency payment; the medical certificate; capital and deposit holdings; the 2023 completed agreement (second holding, excluded); service account_balance 523.11 = sum of the seeded lines. No disconnect notice (medical protection on file), no cash-only status. Automatic clauses checked: no installment beyond 4 is due before 2026-11-01; the single miss does not reach the Hardship default count of 2, so no default obligation is lit.
[Persona] Plain-spoken retired member; volunteers only the wish to pay off and close the plan; phone and membership number on request; passive consent to whatever must be recorded first; runs the payoff herself when handed it; closes when told the plan is paid off. It never mentions September, a shortfall or a miss (no_user_hint).
[Standard solution] Locate by phone, verify with phone + membership number, read service account, agreements, ledgers, bill lines, payments, certificates, capital and deposit records; compute and book the missed installment 3 (2026-09) at 50.58; compute the payoff on the updated ledger 201.67; hand over the payoff tool; the member runs it.
[Verification run] /tmp harness using check_compute.build_env/eval_compute on initial_state, then the real tool for step 11: missed 50.58 with factor baselines 32.95/171.21/0.00/75.58/125.58/70.58, whole baseline 170.95; payoff after the miss 201.67 with factor baselines 151.09/229.85/229.85/211.19, whole baseline 229.85; payoff without the miss 151.09. check_compute --task 0: COMPUTE OK (match True).
[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the published rules alone: the payoff sentence sends the agent to the ledger; installment 3's grace ended 2026-10-01 with 90.00 net credited; the missed-amount rule gives 50.58; the payoff rule then gives 201.67. Agrees with gold.
[Known deviation] The payoff tool closes the arrangement's unbilled balance to zero while billing back the balance less credits applied; the service-side application of those credits and the service bill line the charter's trigger derives are not written by this difficulty's tools (they write arrange tables only). Recorded for the audit.
[Revision round 2 - audit audits/policy_task/payment_arrangement_agreements] T0-F1/D-F1: every result binding now rounds half up exactly (int(x*100 + 0.5 + 1e-6)/100), matching the rule; missed 50.575 -> 50.58, payoff 134.46 (was 50.57/134.45 under float round-half-even); downstream closure figures updated. T0-F2/D-F3: pledge_lookback_by_circumstance relabelled parameter (window length); the payoff's period-count factor replaced by credit_window_by_circumstance, a parameter (window in months), so the payoff keeps 3 parameter + 1 honest method. T0-F3/D-F4a: the deposit-interest credit is now the prior-year interest posted on the January 2026 bill (deposit charter interest_payout_month 1) with 5.60 accrued since; the payoff's credit window is in months and reaches it on the 10-month tier only. D-O4: an unexpired certificate field with no certificate row now falls on the 'no certificate received within those days' tier (sentinel 0000-01-01 instead of today). D-O6: payoff capital_status quotation made verbatim. Re-run: harness missed 50.58 (baselines 32.95/171.21/0.00/75.58/125.58/70.58, whole 170.95), payoff 134.46 (83.88/141.81/229.85/141.81, whole 229.85), payoff without the miss 83.88. [Revision round 3 - audit audits/policy_task/payment_arrangement_agreements] R2-F1: the October capital-retirement credits (138.62 on 2026-10-01, 58.90 on 2025-10-01) are gone; the member's only capital-retirement credit in the window is the 69.24 general retirement of the 2025 resolution (approved 2025-11-18) on the December 2025 bill, as the capital charter pays an active member (bill credit, general_retirement_payment_month 12); the capital account's opened_date is now 1997-06-30, the June allocation (allocation_month 6) of her first patronage year 1996; payable 0. To keep the window on the medical tier reaching a December credit, credit_months_medical is 11 (notice 12, otherwise 1). R2-F3: the Credit Reestablishment Deposit now follows its tier - assessed 2024-07-15 on reconnect_after_nonpay, required 460.00 (twice the highest bill, rounded up to 5), 3 installments (230.00 / 115.00 / 115.00), paid in full 2024-09-24, held 460.00; the January 2026 interest credit is the charter's 2025 interest 460.00 x 2.07% x 365/365 = 9.52; accrued_interest 0.00 (2026 interest accrues on 2026-12-31). The deposit stays held because every monthly refund review since 2026-03-24 (18 months after payment) finds two or more late charges in its 18-month window (2025-08-22 and 2026-03-22, later 2026-06-22) above late_charges_allowed_in_period 1. user_scenario: You are Loretta Vance, sixty-nine, a retired school cook living at 1840 Pleasant Ridge Rd outside Harlan Springs, and you have been a Cedar Fork member since 1996. Back in June you set up a payment plan on your house account after a hard winter, and this morning you made up your mind to be done with it: your nephew paid you for the hay off the back field, and you would rather settle whatever is left on the plan than keep carrying it month to month. You open by saying you would like to pay off your payment plan early and close it out today. When the representative asks who you are, you give your phone number, 2705555318; if they want a second detail you read your membership number off your bill, 0452318. You have only the one house account with the co-op. You do not know the balance on the plan or how it is worked out, and you do not try to guess; you leave the figuring to the representative and go by what the co-op has on file. If the representative explains that something has to be recorded on your account first, you tell them to go ahead and do what they need to. Only if they ask about your husband's oxygen machine or a medical form do you confirm that Dr. Ashworth sent the certificate in September. If they ask what you paid in September, you say you do not recall the amounts and they should go by the co-op's records. When the representative tells you the payoff amount and hands the payoff step over to you, you complete it yourself right then with the amount they gave you; you want to be the one who pays it off, so you do not have the representative do that part for you. Once you hear that the plan is paid off and closed, you thank them warmly and say that was all you needed.

edges.condition: Every installment-billed entry of the agreement whose bill's due date plus missed_installment_grace_days has passed unpaid has a matching arrange_installment_missed entry on arrange_ledger at payoff handling time.
edges.policy_source: The balance billed back on an early payoff is fixed only after every installment of the agreement whose grace period has ended unpaid carries a missed-installment entry on the agreement's ledger.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Installment 3 was billed on the 2026-09-01 bill (due 2026-09-21, Extended Hardship grace 10 days -> grace ended 2026-10-01); payments of 90.00 net of the returned echeck and pledges left it unpaid, yet the agreement's ledger carries no arrange_installment_missed entry at all.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The missed-installment entry for installment 3 (period 2026-09, amount 50.58) lands; missed_month becomes 50.58 and the payoff moves from 151.09 to 201.67.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the payoff waits on the missed-installment entry, so the missed booking (step 11) strictly precedes the payoff (step 13); the reverse order is excluded by the prerequisite sentence and changes the payoff (151.09 instead of 201.67).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the missed-installment write leaves missed_month 0, nothing is covered first and the payoff computes 151.09 instead of 201.67; the terminal ledger also lacks the missed entry.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario only asks to pay off the payment plan early and close it; it never mentions a missed or late installment, September's shortfall, a missed-installment entry or anything to settle first; the only related line is a passive reaction ('If the representative explains that something has to be recorded ... go ahead').
